I have no idea what the pictures are of, they're not El Coyote.
May 2018 • Family
I have read the other reviews and in spite of the fact I live in Nha Trang I am beginning to believe there must be two El Coyote restaurants here or the glowing reviews were written by friends. Like I said in the title the pictures show a rather pleasant, nicely decorated restaurant which is certainly not El Coyote at the address given above. There is not a single decoration in the restaurant that is Mexican. The room is plastered with tacky American Indian pictures and artifacts. The only thing that wasn't American Indian was a Haida Thunderbird dance mask.
I have been there three times and wasn't really pleased with the food any time. Perhaps because I am Mexican and have always ordered the Mexican dishes. This time the tacos were about three inches long and were hard tortillas filled with plain ground beef with a little cheese sprinkled on top. The burritos were soft tortillas filled with plain ground beef with a little cheese sprinkled on top. They tasted identical to each other and nothing like what they were supposed to taste like. My Vietnamese family ordered pizza, perhaps they knew something I didn't. They said the pizzas were quite good and I have to admit my margarita was excellent.

Authentic Cuisine
Apr 2018 • Friends
If you've ever been or have lived deep in the heart of Central or South America, you would know food here is very close to authentic cuisine. Sure, there are a few local substitutions in ingreduents, but the food hasn't lost all of its authenticity by way of the changes. Having lived in Vietnam for 13 years & having experienced the difficulties in finding quality ingredients and having success with much need local substitutions, I would say El Coyote did a superb job! The food brought back fond memories of living in Venezula as a young man. As per service reviews on this place, common, it's a family run business! Get over it and come support El Coyote for who and what they are. Authenticity isn't always the best taste you're expecting, so just come & enjoy it for what it is. Thanks for a great lunch! I will definitely be back. Big Chef Brian.

Authentic Mexican in Vietnam
Feb 2018 • Friends
Two local friends brought me here in late February 2018. I believe El Coyote might have relocated to its present location from elsewhere in Nha Trang. It's not even a five minute ride inland from Tran Phu street, the main beach road.
 The places oozes atmosphere; no corporate Taco Bell here. I've never been to Mexico, but I imagine this is what an authentic Mexican restaurant is like. The server, I believe he may have been the owner, politely served us drinks and the meal and noticing the heat, set up a portable air conditioner nearby. The burrito and other food was really good and the beer was really cold. I had a colloquy with the server/owner after the meal, a highly skilled man socially, and he told me he was from Tijuana, Mexico and L.A.. I guess he knows Mexican restaurants.
 I hadn't enjoyed a cold beer in almost a month since I left the good, old USA; cool or room temperature beer but nothing cold. Until here. And not only was the beer cold, the mugs were frosted! It was the best beer I had in years, redolent of the roofing scene in Shawshank Redemption when the prisoners were rewarded with cold beers on a hot summer day. That good. I'd come here for the beer and not even eat.
Needless to say, I gave our server a workout and he was still friendly as a kitten.
 The bill for three people, food and beer, came to about $20; very reasonable.
 I loved this place. Great atmosphere, congenial personnel, and good food. And cold beer. As Arnold says, "I'll be back."

Food is delicious and well priced.
Mar 2018 • Family
I usually avoid places with low ratings on TripAdvisor but since this place was in a new location and all new reviews looked good I figured it was worth a try. 

First impressions of the place weren’t great. There was no one by the door to greet you and after entering and confirming they were open someone came to help us. The waitresses need to work on their service and be more attentive. These small issues can be remedied was some simple discipline and training of waitstaff. 

I never worry too much about service because I got to a restaurant to eat. Service is important but food is most important. 

We had the empanadas, burritos, fajitas and chili con carne. All of the dishes were made from scratch. There’s no processed foods here. The chili was quite tasty burritos were fresh and my wife loved the empanadas. Fajitas came out sizzling and were good. This place has no issues with the food it simply needs a little passion and heart put back into it. 

Take the one strong point, the food, and build off of it. 

If I owned this restaurant I would do the following. 

1. Clean it extremely thoroughly. 
2. Get some better lighting and adjust the seating so it’s not co fusing where a person should sit. 
3. Train the waitstaff and make sure even when it’s slow that someone is by the door to greet customers get them served a drink and help them order. (To his credit the man who is the manager or owner was quite friendly and took our order)
4. Do some promotions and events like it appears you used to many years ago and build your reputation back. 

Nha Trang needs a good Mexican restaurant and you guys have all the potential to be it. Rise to the occasion. 

I’ll be back for the good food. Thanks for a tasty meal.
